clue.text: Mark with info about old resistance killer of beasts

parts.note: M is short for the mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: about here means the word for info is turned round

parts.note: info means data
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone marks a dossier on an elderly resistance fighter who hunted animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' as M is the old German currency; 'about' here is a reversal signal, not a container, and applies only to the word for info.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter's role is to kill the bull, so he is literally a slayer of animals in the ring.

clue.text: I filmed sir (sic) breaking — a time for worry

indicators.note: breaking signals that the letters of the preceding words are smashed and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note about a knight caught on camera, with an editor's (sic), at an anxious moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle age is proverbially a period of anxious self-doubt about one's life and achievements.

clue.text: Gets on with stories about Calvin Klein brand?

indicators.note: about tells us the word for stories goes round the other piece

parts.note: stories means tales
CK is the brand logo of the fashion house Calvin Klein

explanation.surface: Someone sets to work on tales concerning a famous fashion label.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a job is to set about doing it, to get on with it.

clue.text: Scenery in crude correction

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A rough edit made to a stage set.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre decor is the set and furnishings that form the scenery on stage.

clue.text: Have second thoughts about bums on seats finally

parts.note: about means concerning, which is RE
bums, slang for bottoms, can be asses

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word seats

explanation.surface: A theatre producer reconsiders the importance of filling the auditorium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bums on seats' is a British phrase for paying audience numbers; here 'on' just places ASSES before the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess something is to evaluate it again, reconsidering an earlier judgement.

clue.text: Chap, say, with a wine cellar

parts.note: bod is informal British for a chap or person
say, as in for instance, is EG
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man, for instance, owns a store of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar where wine is stored and sold.

clue.text: Bachelor joins one engineering regiment in old ship

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
one is the Roman numeral I
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A single man enlists in an army engineering unit and serves on an ancient vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme was an ancient galley propelled by two banks of oars.

clue.text: Cutie with a better half away washing in here?

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
taken as written

indicators.note: half away tells us the first half of the word better is dropped

explanation.surface: An attractive person and their spouse are out, perhaps doing the washing-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better half' looks like a spouse, but 'half away' removes BET from 'better', leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty washing-up water is what plates are cleaned in, hence a place for washing.

clue.text: Ogle smashing lady, gee

indicators.note: smashing signals the letters of the next words are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eyes up a gorgeous woman and exclaims in admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' looks like praise for the lady but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amorous or inviting look is a leer or ogle, the stock phrase being to give someone such a look.

clue.text: Floor conservative with locks getting summer seat?

parts.note: a deck is a floor, as on a ship
locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A long-haired Tory knocks someone down and grabs a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding canvas seat is the classic beach or garden chair used in sunny weather.

clue.text: Chanted in Latin? The opposite — vernacular

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other
The opposite reverses the stated order, so Latin goes into the word for chanted

parts.note: chanted means sang

explanation.surface: Monks sang the service in Latin, not the common tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the clue would put SANG inside L; 'The opposite' says put L inside SANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal everyday speech, the colloquial language of ordinary people.

clue.text: Radio carried by man demolishing slums?

definitions.text: Radio carried by man demolishing slums?

parts.words: Radio carried by man demolishing slums?
parts.note: a big portable stereo read whimsically as a person who blows up run-down districts

explanation.definitionFit: A large portable cassette player of the 1980s was carried around playing loud music in the street.

clue.text: I float about moving glider — not good

indicators.note: moving signals that the remaining letters are shifted into a new order
not tells us the letter for good is removed from glider

explanation.surface: A glider pilot drifts aimlessly through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' drops G from GLIDER, leaving LIDER, which 'moving' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer drifts around doing nothing, so the answer can describe itself as one who floats about.

clue.text: Cranky he swore about me being in any other place

indicators.note: about tells us the rearranged letters go round the word me
cranky, meaning eccentric or out of order, signals an anagram

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered man swore at me and wished I were elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cranky' rearranges HE SWORE, and 'about' puts it around ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an unspecified location, any place at all other than here.

clue.text: "Are" (2nd sing) in French, for example, is beginning to trouble writer

parts.note: the French for you are, second person singular, is tu es
say means for example
taken as written

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of trouble

explanation.surface: A grammar note on French verbs gives a writer grief.
explanation.walkthrough: In French, 'you are' (singular, familiar) is 'tu es', giving ES.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist is an author of short prose pieces, a kind of writer.

clue.text: Last thing in gastronomy — fresh sturgeon fry

indicators.note: Last thing in picks the final letter of gastronomy
fresh signals the letters of sturgeon are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: The latest culinary trend is serving freshly caught sturgeon fried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fry' looks like cooking but means young fish, hence young people.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fry, or fry, are young fish and by extension children or young people.

clue.text: Second plane, eg, ending in airport's way

parts.note: a plane is an example of a tree

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of airport

explanation.surface: Another aircraft is approaching the end of the airport's route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests aircraft, but the plane tree is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road, a public way through a town.

clue.text: Craves to include new dig for digs

indicators.note: to include tells us the word for craves takes in the other piece

parts.note: craves means longs

indicators.note: new signals the letters of dig are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a fresh dig to find accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' at the end looks like more of the digging but is the British slang definition; 'new' rearranges the fodder before 'to include' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is British slang for rented rooms, the place where a lodger stays.

clue.text: Cut head off fish, insert a head of garlic and stew

indicators.note: insert tells us the two letters go inside the beheaded fish
Cut head off removes the first letter of the fish

parts.note: a trout is a fish
taken as written

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of garlic

explanation.surface: A recipe: behead the fish, add garlic and stew it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting the head off TROUT leaves ROUT; A and G go in after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a richly seasoned French meat and vegetable stew.

clue.text: Try starting to undercook batter on one fish

parts.note: a go is an attempt or try

indicators.note: starting to picks the first letter of undercook

parts.note: a ram is something that batters, as a battering ram
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: try leaving fish slightly underdone in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: The gourami is a freshwater fish of Asia, often kept in aquariums.

clue.text: I let you in with a flick of the wrist

definitions.text: I let you in with a flick of the wrist

parts.words: I let you in with a flick of the wrist
parts.note: the speaker is a fitting on a door that you turn by hand to open it

explanation.definitionFit: A round handle on a door is turned with a twist of the wrist to open the door.

clue.text: Grandma piercing cloth

parts.note: nan is a familiar word for grandmother
piercing, as a sharp wind or cry, means keen

explanation.surface: A grandmother sticks a needle through fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric originally made in Nanjing.

clue.text: Comparatively stupid I shed light

explanation.surface: A slow-witted person claims to bring enlightenment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimmer means more dull-witted; a dimmer switch is a device that controls how much a lamp illuminates.

clue.text: Son left in street attack running

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for left goes inside the word for a street attack

parts.note: a mugging is a robbery attack in the street

explanation.surface: A boy fled a street robbery in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' looks like fleeing but means running contraband.
explanation.definitionFit: Gun-running or rum-running is illicit carrying of goods across borders.

clue.text: Girl's hair's beginning to turn red due to this

indicators.note: turn signals the letters of the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of hair

explanation.surface: A girl's hair turns red because of this dye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses ANNE plus H (the start of 'hair's') to give the dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish-brown plant dye used to colour hair and skin.

clue.text: I'm said to laugh around noon, yeah possibly

indicators.note: around tells us the rearranged letters go round the letter for noon
possibly signals the letters of yeah could be in another order

explanation.surface: An animal laughs at midday, saying yeah, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges YEAH as HYEA, and 'around' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted scavenger of Africa is famous for its laughing cry.

clue.text: Handle a witty remark and defeat by deceit

explanation.surface: Grip a quip, then cheat someone out of a win.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft is the handle of a tool, a barbed or witty jibe, and in slang to cheat someone badly.

clue.text: Clubs in meantime change filling for pie

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for clubs goes inside the rearranged letters
change signals the letters of meantime are altered in order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: Meanwhile, the card players switch pie fillings.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat is the spiced dried-fruit mixture inside British Christmas mince pies.

clue.text: Reflect on newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror is to reflect an image; the Daily Mirror is a British tabloid paper.

clue.text: What could be moveable bridge?

parts.note: read as something that bridges a gap and can be adjusted, like the tool with movable jaws

explanation.definitionFit: An adjustable wrench spans a nut between its jaws, so it is a thing that spans a gap.
